## Slate context: How has my thinking on religion evolved over the years?

### Background
- **Religion Redefined** — Religion is reframed as any set of foundational assumptions, emotional convictions, and motivating beliefs centered on a person, purpose, or idea — requiring no god, ritual, or institution.
  - Religion comprises the foundational assumptions used in decision-making _(Religion)_
  - Faith transcends fear of supernatural punishment and reward _(Religion)_
  - Religion becomes the prime mover driving daily thoughts and actions _(Religion)_
  - Religion requires no external god or institutional ritual _(Religion)_
- **Religion Critique** — Religion is viewed as a system of fake assumptions and social control that misdirects people from action, promotes withdrawal, yet at its core concerns personal identity and integrity.
  - Religious justification has enabled systematic abuse and violence _(Why am I an anti-theist)_
  - Religion consists of fake assumptions and stupid rituals _(Religion)_
  - Traditional religious practice emphasizes withdrawal and asceticism _(Religion)_
  - Religion misdirects people away from action and achievement _(Religion)_
- **Belief Acquisition** — Belief systems comprising religion, tradition, culture, and moral values are acquired by children through emotional attachment to parents.
  - Belief system comprises religion, tradition, culture, and moral values _(The Right and The Wrong)_
  - Children acquire beliefs through emotional attachment to parents _(The Right and The Wrong)_

### Specifics
### Religion _(2013-07-26)_
- It may be a person, a dream, a purpose, a quest or an idea. Once you start believing in it, once it becomes a part of your life it becomes your religion. The reverence you feel for it, the belief you have in it, the inspiration it provides you is religion.When that one thing becomes your prime mover, when you wake up every day and your first thought is about it. ⚠️ contested
- It’s not about people who sit idle but about those who work to create wonders, people who open new paths to new horizons.
- It is about sticking to the path you chose even in the most adverse conditions. Rituals just let you give that faith an identity, a shape, a figure.Religion is a very important part of decision making.
- Religion is not about going to a temple or a church or a mosque. It’s not about reading Bible or Quran or Geeta daily. It’s not about praying or begging.Religion is a man’s Identity and his integrity.
- It is the tendency to believe, to hold a conviction. It is about having faith in one’s own actions. ⚠️ contested
- When every time you feel lost and your steps start to stagger and that one thing motivates you to keep walking. When every action you perform is another step towards achieving it, when you are assured even in the worst situation that someday you will find it again. Then you can relate all of it to rituals and religion.When you love a person and you think of them in every moment and every action. When you feel their presence even in their absence and still feel motivated and inspired. When their voice makes you feel alive, their presence clears all your mind of all doubts, when even their unrelated words answers all your questions. When you know that whenever you fall they will hold your hand and pick you up, then the reverence you feel for them, the trust you have in them, the faith that they will be always on your side becomes religion and every action of yours becomes a ritual.Once you find your religion in that sense you won’t care about heaven or hell. You will create wonders, you will achieve impossible because you are the immovable object and your religion is the unstoppable force.
- Our Brain always uses a set of assumptions to decide the truth value of a statement. These assumptions make up your religion. If you have a strong faith then your assumptions will be that sure and hence your decision. While being faithless, you will have varying assumptions and hence a staggering decision.It is not necessary to believe in some god or to perform some rituals to have a religion. It is not necessary for your fellow men to believe same as you to hold a faith. Each and every man has his own religion, his integrity. When you love something or someone with a conviction then that becomes your religion. ⚠️ contested
- I have been an atheist for a long time religion being a set of fake assumptions and stupid rituals. It’s still impossible for me to conceive an idea of a super power that controls everything. I always saw religion as a failed attempt at science. To me Religion was a method to control men, to make them perform an action without ever questioning it. Religion was heaven and hell misguiding men out of action. Religious people were those saints who leave everything behind to live in forests and caves, those who beg in the name of god and find it a rightful thing to do. Those who suggest earning money is sin, all the desires and actions towards them are sin.But in recent days I realized religion is more than sacred books and rituals. ⚠️ contested

### Perturbation of opinion _(2017-06-25)_
- We all have heard or experienced the motherly love.
- Even the foremost source of information, the mother and the teachers. And these opinions we receive are slowly embedded in our character over time and can form our opinions about things as simple as food we eat to as complex as what we perceive is good for the country. Hence it is essential that we verify every piece of information we receive and ensure that we separate the opinion from the facts and then form our own opinion from these facts.

query: Summarise my views on AI and memory systems.
key_facts: Memory is the next paradigm shift in AI — it becomes the moat via switching cost
Current memory structures (snippets, chats) are insufficient; memory must be hierarchical or graph-based
Debugging is the real test of AI coding — where things fail and how fast you find what broke
A concept-then-residual approach: match high-level concepts, subtract them as background, focus on what is novel

## Slate context: Summarise my views on AI and memory systems.

### Background
- **AI Hierarchical Memory** — LLMs lack native hierarchical memory, but building it for AI is technically achievable and implemented by projects like Human Layer through a hierarchical context layer.
  - Building hierarchical memory for AI is technically achievable _(Hierarchical Context for AI Development)_
  - Human Layer project implements this through a hierarchical context layer _(Hierarchical Context for AI Development)_
  - Background concepts are filtered to highlight novelty _(RAG Limitations and hierarchical memory)_
  - LLMs do not implement hierarchical memory natively _(Hierarchical Context for AI Development)_
- **AI Impact on Engineering** — AI is viewed as a tool analogous to prior technologies that reduces repetitive work, shifts software engineers toward planning and architecture, and raises contested questions about its relevance for coding and product building through human-AI collaboration mirroring professional hierarchies.
  - AI is fundamentally like previous technologies _(There is this debate around how relevant AI agents are espec)_
  - AI reduces repetitive work _(There is this debate around how relevant AI agents are espec)_
  - AI agent relevance for coding and product building is contested _(There is this debate around how relevant AI agents are espec)_
  - Software engineers shift from coding to planning and architecture _(There is this debate around how relevant AI agents are espec)_
- **Brain Memory and Learning** — The brain manages limited memory by selectively storing minimised representations, reinforcing frequently used memories through repetition, and using partial matches against stored elements to interpret new information.

### Black box approach to the brain _(2017-11-29)_
- Our brain does a lot of things and has a very complex structure. When trying to build an artificial intelligence, scientists have been trying to emulate the structure of the brain. Our brain has evolved over millions of years of life. The very specific structure is so because of that evolutionary process and if we want to emulate the structure we need to emulate the process of evolution.
- The kid is not calculating where the next step will fall, it just keeps on moving. Things which achieve a goal are repeated more as compared to the ones that don’t.
- It is quite evident that people’s judgement and behaviour is very much guided by their personal experiences. That is the kind of events that happened around them, defines what their brain deems important.
- At this point we may ask what if we didn’t have this bias. This problem of limited memory and hence the idea of relevance or importance playing against us. Will it make us more objective or intelligent? Apart from the brain’s limitation, we are also limited by what we observe and what we can do. These limitations hence also play in building our biases. At the same time these limitations lead to imagination. When we can take only one action and it is extremely important we play out different scenarios in our head, thinking ahead multiple steps.
- But what we need to ask ourselves is if there exists another way to achieve the goal? The goal here is to emulate the intelligence. If we could find out what makes us intelligent without going into the structural details of the brain we may emulate intelligence without emulating the structure. Let’s consider the brain a black box and look at what the box does.
- A baby just born doesn’t do much and most probably doesn’t think much too. For a child hence most of the thought processing is observation and action. It stores the observations in its head which becomes its memory and then simply repeat it again and again until it learns something. Most of such thought is what we call subconscious thinking.
- They have to go to therapy to get up to speed. This further establishes the point that our brain focuses on what it does repeatedly and looses track of other things. But this shouldn’t make us intelligent, but probably is a drawback of our brain. But come to think of it, the amount of data that flows in and out of our brain if it all had stayed in our brain it would get full pretty fast. Hence it is necessary to minimize the memory somehow. Clearing out the noise and keeping only the important aspects hence is a necessity of our brain. But an important question is does it somehow makes us smart/intelligent? If we had infinite memory we would have memorized each and everything and whenever it appeared in future we would have simply repeated what we did then.
- It takes input from specified sources (organs) and relays outputs to specified organs. It sounds absurd considering the amount of thoughts it handles everyday but deep down that is the core functionality the brain does. You can then ask what suddenly made humanity a lot smarter than rest of animals with brains. Well clearly the number of thoughts we process, our tendency to play events in our heads and of course our emotions.
- When to change gear, when to apply breaks, when to press clutch. But as we drive more and more, our hands are legs get automatically synced to the environment around us and we can make those decisions without any conscious thought. From all of above it can be easily concluded that the most important aspect of our brain is identifying relations between stored information and incoming data. More relations a brain can identify smarter it is. It makes a brain more creative and hence intelligent.
